content.text: Tenosynovitis denotes irritation of a tendon within a tendon sheath. Tendon sheaths are found in areas where tendons cross over bones or bony prominences.
The tendinous sheath of the FPL muscle (sometimes called the radial bursa) begins just proximal to the carpal tunnel before angling around the scaphoid and trapezium to the thumb.

items: Overuse condition with gradual onset
Main complaint is pain
Pain most commonly at A1 pulley — at the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb

content.text: Palmar thumb pain, most commonly reported after an activity requiring thumb movement.

With tenosynovitis, irritation is between the tendon and the sheath. Therefore, AROM is usually more provocative than MMT or RROM because the tendon is pulled through the sheath during movement. Most provoking of all is resisted concentric testing (movement with load).

items: Gripping
Rock climbing
Texting

content.text: FPL tenosynovitis sometimes occurs following internal fixation of a radius fracture.

items: Is this a new activity, or recent change or sudden increase in activity?
AROM of thumb movement is painful, especially flexion and extension. A clicking may be present
Isometric testing (e.g. RROM) is often pain-free
Muscle shortening is not common
Muscle weakness is not common — testing FPL or FPB may rule out strain
UCL & RCL of the 1st MCP may be used to rule out ligament sprain
Any task requiring significant thumb movement is likely to cause pain
Reduce or temporarily remove provoking factor
Taping or splinting may be used
NSAIDs and hydrotherapy may help
Isometrics are safe to perform
Avoid exercises requiring thumb movement (tendon excursion through sheath)

content.text: A good guideline for progression: the patient is ready for AROM or concentric exercises once able to perform 10 repetitions of 60-second isometric holds without symptoms.

items: Reduce adhesions around the tendon sheath
Promote normal resting muscle tone of the affected muscle
Promote normal joint play and reduced fascial restrictions in area
Treat compensatory structures to restore overall function
Reduce adhesions around FPL tendon sheath with skin rolling and MFR
Promote normal resting muscle tone of FPL using segmental muscle stripping, petrissage, and origin-insertion
Maintain neuromuscular control with gentle isometric muscle setting
Decrease TrP activity in muscles in the area based on presentation
Decrease tension in anterior forearm with forearm flexor MFR and petrissage
Restore normal joint play with metacarpal and carpal joint play and radiocarpal mobilisations
Reduce fascial restriction with intercompartmental MFR

content.title: Cautions
content.text: Do not friction or put direct pressure down into the FPL tendon sheath. Avoid active or passive movement of the thumb unless clearly pain-free. Avoid heat directly over the tendon sheath which may be inflamed.

Expected timelines are highly variable. It is very difficult to offload the thumb as it is used in so many vital ADLs. Adherence to modifications and protection of the area are most important in determining the timeline for recovery.
Mild cases in adherent individuals may be cleared up in 10-21 days in the best case scenarios.

A clinical impression for tenosynovitis should include: affected tendon, severity, and whether chronic or flared-up. Example: 'Consistent with FPL tenosynovitis of mild severity in the flare-up state.'

quiz.question: In FPL tenosynovitis, which type of muscle testing is usually MORE provocative?
quiz.explanation: AROM is usually more provocative than RROM because during active movement the tendon is pulled through the irritated sheath. The most provoking is resisted concentric testing (movement with load).

quiz.question: What is a good guideline for when a patient with FPL tenosynovitis is ready to progress to AROM exercises?
options: After 2 weeks of rest regardless of symptoms
When able to perform 10 reps of 60-second isometric holds without symptoms
When PROM is full and pain-free
quiz.explanation: The patient is ready for AROM or concentric exercises once able to perform 10 repetitions of 60-second isometric holds without symptoms.

quiz.question: Heat should be applied directly over the FPL tendon sheath to reduce inflammation.
quiz.explanation: Avoid heat directly over the tendon sheath which may be inflamed. This is listed as a specific caution in the treatment guidelines.
